z_crit * se_p, p + z_crit * se_p),     back_transformed = t(       apply(p_draws, 2L, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))     )   ) }  # Both routes need an interior estimate: on a face the ILR chart # diverges and the information in rho is singular. interior <- apply(p_hat, 2L, min) > 1e-6 routes <- lapply(which(interior), function(i) interval_routes(p_hat[, i]))  summarise_route <- function(name) {   lower <- sapply(routes, function(r) r[[name]][, 1])   upper <- sapply(routes, function(r) r[[name]][, 2])   data.frame(     route = name,     cell_type = names(p_true),     coverage = rowMeans(lower <= p_true & p_true <= upper),     outside_unit_interval = rowMeans(lower < 0 | upper > 1),     median_width = apply(upper - lower, 1L, median)   ) } route_summary <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(c("delta", "back_transformed"), summarise_route) ) rownames(route_summary) <- NULL knitr::kable(route_summary, digits = 3)

z_crit * se_p, p + z_crit * se_p),     back_transformed = t(       apply(p_draws, 2L, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))     )   ) }  # Both routes need an interior estimate: on a face the ILR chart # diverges and the information in rho is singular. interior <- apply(p_hat, 2L, min) > 1e-6 routes <- lapply(which(interior), function(i) interval_routes(p_hat[, i]))  summarise_route <- function(name) {   lower <- sapply(routes, function(r) r[[name]][, 1])   upper <- sapply(routes, function(r) r[[name]][, 2])   data.frame(     route = name,     cell_type = names(p_true),     coverage = rowMeans(lower <= p_true & p_true <= upper),     outside_unit_interval = rowMeans(lower < 0 | upper > 1),     median_width = apply(upper - lower, 1L, median)   ) } route_summary <- do.call(   rbind,   lapply(c("delta", "back_transformed"), summarise_route) ) rownames(route_summary) <- NULL knitr::kable(route_summary, digits = 3)

centre) / scale Sigma_star <- Sigma for (j in seq_len(2)) {   Sigma_star[, , j] <- Sigma[, , j] * tcrossprod(D_inv) } p_star <- deconvolute_ratios_Marquardt_Levenberg(   drop(y_star),   mu_star,   Sigma_star,   itmax = 80 ) fit_z <- fit_decovart(   mu,   y,   Sigma = Sigma,   method = "Marquardt-Levenberg",   itmax = 80,   standardise = TRUE )  rbind(   raw = drop(coef(fit_raw)),   general_affine = p_star,   gene_wise_z = drop(coef(fit_z)) ) #>                      ct1       ct2 #> raw            0.6489623 0.3510377 #> general_affine 0.6489623 0.3510377 #> gene_wise_z    0.6489623 0.3510377 set.seed(2) p_true <- c(0.6, 0.4) y0 <- matrix(drop(mu %*% p_true), ncol = 1, dimnames = list(genes, "s1")) y_pert <- y0 + rnorm(3, sd = 0.2)  Sigma_diag <- Sigma for (j in 1:2) {   Sigma_diag[, , j] <- diag(diag(Sigma[, , j])) } # GLS competitor: mean-only fit with the fixed diagonal residual covariance # diag{Sigma(p_true)}, which does not move with the estimate. w_gls <- diag(diag(.compute_global_variance(p_true, Sigma))) gls_fixed <- function(y, mu, W) {   w_inv_mu <- solve(W, mu)   p_hat <- drop(solve(crossprod(mu, w_inv_mu), crossprod(w_inv_mu, y)))   repair_simplex(stats::setNames(p_hat, colnames(mu))) }  fit_spec <- function(y, S) {   drop(coef(fit_decovart(     mu,     y,     Sigma = S,     method = "Marquardt-Levenberg",     itmax = 80   ))) }  est <- cbind(   full = fit_spec(y_pert, Sigma),   celltype_diagonal = fit_spec(y_pert, Sigma_diag),   gls_fixed = gls_fixed(drop(y_pert), mu, w_gls) ) rmse <- apply(est, 2, function(p_hat) sqrt(mean((p_hat - p_true)^2))) list(estimates = est, rmse_to_truth = rmse) #> $estimates #>          full celltype_diagonal gls_fixed #> ct1 0.6112459         0.6112459 0.6121588 #> ct2 0.3887541         0.3887541 0.3878412 #>  #> $rmse_to_truth #>              full celltype_diagonal         gls_fixed  #>        0.01124588        0.01124588        0.01215877 seeds <- c(11L, 22L, 33L) starts <- lapply(seeds, function(s) {   set.seed(s)   starting_simplex(2L, "dirichlet", nms = cts) }) names(starts) <- paste0("seed_", seeds)  fit_from_start <- function(fun, p0) {   fun(drop(y_pert), mu, Sigma, itmax = 80, initial_p = p0) }  ml <- vapply(   starts,   function(p0) fit_from_start(deconvolute_ratios_Marquardt_Levenberg, p0),   numeric(2) ) nr <- vapply(   starts,   function(p0) fit_from_start(deconvolute_ratios_Newton_Raphson, p0),   numeric(2) ) list(   starts = starts,   marquardt = ml,   newton_raphson = nr ) #> $starts #> $starts$seed_11 #>        ct1        ct2  #> 0.09319046 0.90680954  #>  #> $starts$seed_22 #>       ct1       ct2  #> 0.2746408 0.7253592  #>  #> $starts$seed_33 #>       ct1       ct2  #> 0.1712805 0.8287195  #>  #>  #> $marquardt #>      seed_11   seed_22   seed_33 #> ct1 0.611246 0.6112463 0.6112459 #> ct2 0.388754 0.3887537 0.3887541 #>  #> $newton_raphson #>      seed_11  seed_22  seed_33 #> ct1 0.611246 0.611246 0.611246 #> ct2 0.388754 0.388754 0.388754

code: # ----------------------------------------------------------------- # SECTION 1: GENERATIVE MODEL # Build precision matrices for each (G, structure) combination # ----------------------------------------------------------------- SEED <- 20260807L  G_grid     <- c(20L, 50L, 100L, 250L, 500L) structures <- c("dense", "banded", "block_diagonal", "low_rank")  build_precision <- function(G, structure, seed = SEED) {   set.seed(seed)   switch(structure,     dense        = build_normalised_precision(       generate_random_network_skeleton(G, model = "erdos_renyi", seed = seed)     ),     banded       = {       adj <- bandSparse(G, G, k = -3:3, symmetric = TRUE,                         diagonals = replicate(7, rep(1, G), simplify = FALSE))       diag(adj) <- 0       build_normalised_precision(as.matrix(adj))     },     block_diagonal = {       block_size <- G %/% 4L       adj_block  <- Matrix::bdiag(         replicate(4L, {           generate_random_network_skeleton(block_size, model = "erdos_renyi",                                           seed = seed)         }, simplify = FALSE)       )       build_normalised_precision(as.matrix(adj_block))     },     low_rank     = {       # D + U C U^T structure (rank 5 perturbation)       D_vals <- stats::runif(G, 0.5, 2)       U_mat  <- matrix(rnorm(G * 5L), G, 5L)       diag(D_vals) + tcrossprod(U_mat) * 0.1     }   ) }  precision_grids <- tidyr::expand_grid(G = G_grid, structure = structures) |>   dplyr::mutate(     Omega = purrr::map2(G, structure, build_precision)   )

code: # ----------------------------------------------------------------- # SECTION 2: INFERENCE / TIMING # Compare solve(Omega, v) using different backends # ----------------------------------------------------------------- N_TIMING <- 50L dir.create("output/supp_S2", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)  benchmark_results <- precision_grids |>   dplyr::mutate(timing = purrr::map2(G, Omega, \(g, Om) {     v <- rnorm(g)     backends <- list(       dense_cholesky  = \() solve(Om, v),       block_diagonal  = \() {         chol_Om <- chol(Om)         backsolve(chol_Om, forwardsolve(t(chol_Om), v))       }     )     purrr::map_dfr(backends, \(fn) {       times <- replicate(N_TIMING, system.time(fn())[["elapsed"]])       list(mean_ms = mean(times) * 1e3, sd_ms = sd(times) * 1e3)     }, .id = "backend")   })) |>   tidyr::unnest(timing)  saveRDS(benchmark_results, "output/supp_S2/inversion_timing.rds")

code: # ----------------------------------------------------------------- # SECTION 1: GENERATIVE MODEL # Build true Sigma matrices and compute mis-specified alternatives # ----------------------------------------------------------------- SEED <- 20260807L G <- 50L J <- 3L  cov_models_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(   cosine_mu   = c(0.0, 0.5, 0.9),   cov_model   = c("true_full", "ct_diagonal", "global_diagonal", "identity") ) |>   dplyr::mutate(scenario_id = dplyr::row_number())  build_true_cov <- function(G, J, seed = SEED) {   purrr::map(seq_len(J), \(j) {     net <- generate_random_network_skeleton(G,       model = "erdos_renyi",       seed = seed + j     )     build_normalised_precision(net) |> solve()   }) }  true_covs <- build_true_cov(G, J, SEED)  # Mis-specified alternatives ct_diag_covs <- purrr::map(true_covs, \(Sigma) diag(diag(Sigma)))  # Global weighted diagonal D_global = diag( sum_j (1/J^2) Sigma_j ) D_global_vec <- Reduce(`+`, purrr::map(true_covs, \(S) S / J^2)) |>   diag() global_diag_covs <- purrr::map(seq_len(J), \(.) diag(D_global_vec))  identity_covs <- purrr::map(seq_len(J), \(.) diag(G))  cov_specs <- list(   true_full       = true_covs,   ct_diagonal     = ct_diag_covs,   global_diagonal = global_diag_covs,   identity        = identity_covs )

title: Appendix S5 — Model Mis-specification (Description Only)
text: DeCovarT model assumes bulk expression arises Gaussian convolution: one latent profile per cell type, \boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}\sim\mathcal{N}_G(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j), weighted p_j summed, \boldsymbol{y} \sim \mathcal{N}_G\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\;   \sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\Bigr). Real bulk RNA-seq violates assumption least five ways: Observation noise model: counts follow negative binomial (NB) Poisson-log-normal (PLN) distribution rather Gaussian. Heavy-tailed contaminated bulk: outlier samples (technical artefacts, cell doublets) inflate tails. Missing reference component: unmodelled cell type contributes bulk; estimated proportions redistributed. Inter-sample (copula) correlations: genes share latent batch structure, inducing correlation across observations. Wrong covariance reference: within-cell-type covariance \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j estimated different cohort technology, introducing systematic bias.

code: # Fitness of a soft gene mask: condition number of the mean signature # and average MixSim overlap of the type laws on the selected genes. # mu: G0 x J means; Sigma: list of J covariance matrices (G0 x G0). panel_fitness <- function(mask, mu, Sigma, threshold = 0.5) {   g <- which(mask > threshold)   if (length(g) < ncol(mu)) {     return(c(Inf, Inf))   }   kappa_g <- kappa(mu[g, , drop = FALSE], exact = TRUE)   ov <- MixSim::overlap(     Pi = rep(1 / ncol(mu), ncol(mu)),     Mu = t(mu[g, , drop = FALSE]),     S = simplify2array(lapply(Sigma, function(A) A[g, g, drop = FALSE]))   )   c(kappa_g, ov$BarOmega) }  pareto <- mco::nsga2(   fn = panel_fitness,   idim = nrow(mu),   odim = 2,   mu = mu,   Sigma = Sigma,   lower.bounds = rep(0, nrow(mu)),   upper.bounds = rep(1, nrow(mu)),   popsize = 100,   generations = 50 ) # pareto$value: objectives; pareto$par: masks; pareto$pareto.optimal candidates <- expand.grid(   x1 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11),   x2 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11) ) design <- skpr::gen_design(   candidateset = candidates,   model = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   trials = 20,   optimality = "D",   repeats = 100 ) skpr::get_optimality(design, "D") result <- AlgDesign::optFederov(   formula = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   data = candidates,   nTrials = 20,   criterion = "D",   nRepeats = 100 ) result$D # Robust D-score of a gene panel over composition scenarios. # information_by_gene[[s]] is a list over genes of the (J-1) x (J-1) # contributions to I_G(p_s); summing them assumes a diagonal covariance. # With a full covariance, recompute I_G(p_s) on the panel instead. d_objective <- function(selected, information_by_gene, ridge = 1e-8) {   scores <- vapply(information_by_gene, function(info_s) {     info <- Reduce(`+`, info_s[selected])     info <- info + diag(ridge, nrow(info))     as.numeric(determinant(info, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus)   }, numeric(1))   min(scores) }  greedy_d <- function(candidates, information_by_gene, size) {   selected <- integer(0)   for (step in seq_len(size)) {     pool <- setdiff(candidates, selected)     gain <- vapply(pool, function(g) {       d_objective(c(selected, g), information_by_gene)     }, numeric(1))     selected <- c(selected, pool[which.max(gain)])   }   selected }

code: # Fitness of a soft gene mask: condition number of the mean signature # and average MixSim overlap of the type laws on the selected genes. # mu: G0 x J means; Sigma: list of J covariance matrices (G0 x G0). panel_fitness <- function(mask, mu, Sigma, threshold = 0.5) {   g <- which(mask > threshold)   if (length(g) < ncol(mu)) {     return(c(Inf, Inf))   }   kappa_g <- kappa(mu[g, , drop = FALSE], exact = TRUE)   ov <- MixSim::overlap(     Pi = rep(1 / ncol(mu), ncol(mu)),     Mu = t(mu[g, , drop = FALSE]),     S = simplify2array(lapply(Sigma, function(A) A[g, g, drop = FALSE]))   )   c(kappa_g, ov$BarOmega) }  pareto <- mco::nsga2(   fn = panel_fitness,   idim = nrow(mu),   odim = 2,   mu = mu,   Sigma = Sigma,   lower.bounds = rep(0, nrow(mu)),   upper.bounds = rep(1, nrow(mu)),   popsize = 100,   generations = 50 ) # pareto$value: objectives; pareto$par: masks; pareto$pareto.optimal

title: Appendix S6 — Synthetic scenario for comparing gene-screening strategies
text: Strategy F maximises robust D-criterion 3.1 composition grid. Standard design packages work factor grid: skpr (D, , E, G, criteria) AlgDesign::optFederov() (Fedorov exchange) (Wheeler 2025). Neither implements composition-dependent information DeCovarT, F uses custom objective greedy exchange search. two package calls illustrate standard D-optimal designs .
code: candidates <- expand.grid(   x1 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11),   x2 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11) ) design <- skpr::gen_design(   candidateset = candidates,   model = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   trials = 20,   optimality = "D",   repeats = 100 ) skpr::get_optimality(design, "D") result <- AlgDesign::optFederov(   formula = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   data = candidates,   nTrials = 20,   criterion = "D",   nRepeats = 100 ) result$D # Robust D-score of a gene panel over composition scenarios. # information_by_gene[[s]] is a list over genes of the (J-1) x (J-1) # contributions to I_G(p_s); summing them assumes a diagonal covariance. # With a full covariance, recompute I_G(p_s) on the panel instead. d_objective <- function(selected, information_by_gene, ridge = 1e-8) {   scores <- vapply(information_by_gene, function(info_s) {     info <- Reduce(`+`, info_s[selected])     info <- info + diag(ridge, nrow(info))     as.numeric(determinant(info, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus)   }, numeric(1))   min(scores) }  greedy_d <- function(candidates, information_by_gene, size) {   selected <- integer(0)   for (step in seq_len(size)) {     pool <- setdiff(candidates, selected)     gain <- vapply(pool, function(g) {       d_objective(c(selected, g), information_by_gene)     }, numeric(1))     selected <- c(selected, pool[which.max(gain)])   }   selected }

text: Constrained DeCovarT maps unconstrained coordinates \boldsymbol{\rho}_{}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1} cellular proportions \boldsymbol{p}_{} open simplex via regularised soft-max \boldsymbol{\psi}, forms bulk observation Gaussian convolution cell-type profiles \boldsymbol{x}_{j}\sim\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}): \boldsymbol{y}_{}\,|\,\cdot \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\Bigl(   \boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}_{},\;   \sum_{j=1}^{J}p_{ji}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j} \Bigr). diagram shows constrained graphical model. Forward map \boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p} (C^{2}-diffeomorphism): p_{j}=\frac{e^{\rho_{j}}}{\sum_{k<J}e^{\rho_{k}}+1}\ (j<J),\qquad p_{J}=\frac{1}{\sum_{k<J}e^{\rho_{k}}+1},\qquad \boldsymbol{\psi}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{p})=\bigl(\ln(p_{j}/p_{J})\bigr)_{j<J}.

what: Chi-bar-square tail probability for boundary likelihood-ratio tests — chi_bar_square_pvalue
title: Chi-bar-square tail probability for boundary likelihood-ratio tests — chi_bar_square_pvalue
text: Upper-tail probability mixture $$   \bar{\chi}^{2}   =   \sum_{=0}^{q}   w_i\,\chi^{2}_{s+},   \qquad   w_i=\binom{q}{}2^{-q}, $$ \(q\) constraints active boundary parameter space \(s\) interior constraints. Case 9 (Self Liang 1987) , generalises \(\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{1}\) result (Chernoff 1954) . \(q=0\) mixture collapses ordinary \(\chi^{2}_{s}\) (Wilks 1938) .

Supply weights explicitly, calibrate simulation bootstrap_decovart(), whenever \(q>1\) constrained cell types share signal.

title: Chi-bar-square tail probability for boundary likelihood-ratio tests — chi_bar_square_pvalue
text: \(\chi^{2}_{0}\) point mass origin, strict upper tail \(\Pr(\chi^{2}_{0}>D)\) zero every \(D\ge 0\). component therefore removes weight: one active constraint interior constraint p-value \(\tfrac{1}{2}\Pr(\chi^{2}_{1}>D)\), capped \(0.5\) \(D=0\). Note stats::pchisq() switches closed tail exactly q = 0 df = 0; strict convention used p-value stays continuous statistic.

ISSN 0162-1459. doi:10.1080/01621459.1987.10478472 . Chernoff H (1954). “Distribution Likelihood Ratio.” Annals Mathematical Statistics, 25(3), 573–578. ISSN 0003-4851. doi:10.1214/aoms/1177728725 . what: Average pairwise Jeffreys divergence of a Gaussian mixture — compute_average_jeffreys
title: Average pairwise Jeffreys divergence of a Gaussian mixture — compute_average_jeffreys
text: Returns \(p_j p_{\ell}\)-weighted mean pairwise Jeffreys (symmetrised KL) divergences purified Gaussians, closed form multivariate-normal Kullback–Leibler divergence (https://statproofbook.github.io/P/mvn-kl.html) $$   \overline{J}   =   \frac{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}\, J(f_{j},f_{\ell})   }{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}   }   \[0,\infty), $$ \(f_{j}=\mathcal{N}_{G}(   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j} )\). p omitted defaults equi-balanced vector \(1/J\), recovers uniform pairwise average \(2/(J(J-1))\sum_{j<\ell}J(f_{j},f_{\ell})\).

what: Score mean profiles with AutoGeneS-style objectives — compute_mean_profile_objectives
title: Score mean profiles with AutoGeneS-style objectives — compute_mean_profile_objectives
text: Computes two objectives used AutoGeneS signature quality. columns \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\) \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\), cosine (angle similarity, akin Pearson correlation centred, unit-norm vectors without mean-centring—\(\ell_2\) normalisation) $$   \cos(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k})   =   \frac{     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2\,     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   }, $$ Euclidean separation $$   \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   =   \sqrt{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2^{2}     +\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2^{2}     -2\,     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }. $$ returned scores mean absolute pairwise cosine (minimise) sum pairwise Euclidean distances (maximise).

what: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
title: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
text: probability vector \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\) \(J\) classes (: cell types), Shannon entropy $$   H(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j \log p_j, $$ convention \(0\log 0 = 0\). Dividing maximum entropy \(\log J\) (uniform \(J\) classes) yields normalised Shannon entropy $$   H^{\star}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   \frac{H(\boldsymbol{p})}{\log J}   \[0,1], $$ \(H^{\star}=0\) Dirac mass one type \(H^{\star}=1\) uniform distribution \(J\) cell types. Zero masses dropped inside sum; normaliser still uses original class count \(J\). preferable changing logarithm base number positive masses \(J'\), renormalise support hide sparsity relative full panel cell types.

what: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
title: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
text: Estimates \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}=\arg\max_{\boldsymbol{p}} \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})\) Gaussian convolution model $$   \boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})   \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\bigr),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j, $$ subject simplex constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1\), \(\boldsymbol{p}\ge\mathbf{0}\). title: Fit the DeCovarT Gaussian-convolution model — fit_decovart
text: Standardisation. CIBERSORT requires non-negative expression, missing values, non-log linear scale (Newman et al. 2015) . logarithm concave, Jensen's inequality shifts first second moments \(\log(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\neq(\log\boldsymbol{\mu})\boldsymbol{p}\). gene-wise affine map \(\boldsymbol{x}\mapsto D^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{m})\) \(D,\boldsymbol{m}\) \(\boldsymbol{Y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j^\star=D^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j D^{-1}\) leaves MLE \(\boldsymbol{p}\) unchanged (equivariance). Wald covariance. Let \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). expected Fisher information unconstrained mean–covariance map (multivariate normal; see e.g. Wikipedia entry Fisher information, multivariate normal) $$   (\boldsymbol{p})_{jk}   =   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\top}   \boldsymbol{\Omega}(\boldsymbol{p})   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   +   2 p_j p_k\,   \mathrm{tr}\bigl(     \boldsymbol{\Omega}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j     \boldsymbol{\Omega}(\boldsymbol{p})\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k   \bigr). $$ Cramer–Rao gives \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{z}})\succeq I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}\) ILR coordinates, \(I_{\boldsymbol{z}} =\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\top} (\boldsymbol{p}) \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\) \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})\mathbf{V}\) (jacobian_isometric_logistic()). delta method maps bound back simplex: $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}. $$

Evaluated log-sum-exp shift large \(\|\boldsymbol{z}\|\) overflow. $$   \boldsymbol{z}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\log\boldsymbol{p}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\operatorname{clr}(\boldsymbol{p}), $$ well-defined \(\mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{1}=0\). Requires strictly positive composition (open simplex).

title: Unconstrained DeCovarT log-likelihood — loglik_multivariate
text: additive constant independent \(\boldsymbol{p}\), $$   \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})   -\tfrac{1}{2}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})^{\mathsf{T}}   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}   (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}). $$ Computationally Cholesky--backsolve evaluation mvtnorm::dmvnorm(..., log = TRUE) (Genz Bretz), omitting additive \(-\tfrac{G}{2}\log(2\pi)\) depend \(\boldsymbol{p}\). cached factor .sigma_p_factorisation() supplies upper-triangular \(\boldsymbol{R}\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{R}\); Mahalanobis term \(\lVert\boldsymbol{R}^{-\mathsf{T}} (\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p})\rVert^{2}\), obtained base::backsolve() without forming explicit inverse. inverse still cached analytic score Hessian need \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}(\boldsymbol{p}) =\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\). QR factorisation \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\) expensive route SPD quantities; Cholesky natural factorisation. Argument mean_signature_matrix stores plug-mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\). Latent sample-specific profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}\) observed; frequentist likelihood treats \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) fixed proxy. Estimating latents jointly \(\boldsymbol{p}\) requires Bayesian / MAP step (see .map_gaussian_convolution()).

title: Likelihood-ratio test for cellular ratios — lrt_decovart
text: Interior null. every tested ratio lies strictly inside \((0,1)\), \(D\) asymptotically \(\chi^{2}_{||}\) (Wilks 1938) . Boundary null. null \(p_j=0\) lets parameter move one direction , local parameter space half-line rather vector space Wilks' theorem fails. limit chi-bar-square mixture chi_bar_square_pvalue(): single active constraint, \(D\rightsquigarrow\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{0}+\tfrac{1}{2}\chi^{2}_{1}\) Chernoff (1954) , generalised several active constraints Self Liang (1987) . Boundary calibration selected automatically tested value within boundary_tol 0, tested values sum one, forces every ratio zero (null \(p_j=1\) fixes \(J-1\) coordinates faces); override n_boundary. binomial weights chi_bar_square_pvalue() exact orthogonal constraints; several correlated faces approximate weights tangent cone, bootstrap_decovart() null_value gives calibration rely . Replication. calibrations population statements: need replicate bulk samples genuinely share one composition \(\boldsymbol{p}\). single \(G\)-vector supplies replication (genes dependent \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\), adding bulk samples distinct compositions adds parameters fast observations). Pass several replicate columns y, calibrate bootstrap_decovart().

what: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
title: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
text: bootstrap sample \(=1,\ldots,N\), draws latent purified profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\sim   \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) independently cell type \(j=1,\ldots,J\), forms bulk linear convolution $$   \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }   =\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\boldsymbol{p}   =\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}, $$ matching article's conditional model \(\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})\sim \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}))\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})= \sum_j p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\). mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) shared across samples; latent draws \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\) vary \(\). Stacking draws three-way array \(\mathcal{X}=(x_{gji})\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J\times N}\), bulk matrix mode-2 tensor–vector contraction $$   \boldsymbol{Y}   =\mathcal{X}\times_{2}\boldsymbol{p},   \qquad   y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}x_{gji}\,p_{j}   \quad(g=1,\ldots,G;\; =1,\ldots,N), $$ sample recovers \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\,\boldsymbol{p}\) \(\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\).

what: Cramer–Rao / ILR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_ilr_delta
title: Cramer–Rao / ILR delta-method covariance of \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}\) — vcov_ilr_delta
text: Maps expected Fisher information unconstrained proportions isometric log-ratio (ILR) chart back simplex via delta method. Let \(\boldsymbol{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{V}\boldsymbol{z})\) Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}=\mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p}) \mathbf{V}\) (jacobian_isometric_logistic()). Fisher information transforms $$   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}   =   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   =   \mathbf{V}^{\mathsf{T}}   \mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})   (\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{S}(\boldsymbol{p})   \mathbf{V}. $$ first-order delta method yields $$   \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}})   \approx   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}   I_{\boldsymbol{z}}^{-1}   \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}^{\mathsf{T}}. $$ simplex covariance invariant orthogonal rotations \(\mathbf{V}\). construction undefined simplex boundary (log-ratio chart blows ); function returns NA warning. Wald intervals vcov.decovart_fit(), confint.decovart_fit() deconvolute_ratios() use expected-Fisher ILR map. observed Hessian hessian_loglik_constrained() Newton steps ; Wald covariance.
